title: Developers
tokensDescription: Create scoped tokens for scripts and integrations. A token acts on behalf of the member who created it and is limited by their current role.
createTokenDescription: Select only the scopes this integration needs. The token is shown once.
name: Name
oneTimeDescription: This is the only time you will see this token. Store it in your secret manager now.
revokeDescription: Requests using this token will fail immediately. This cannot be undone.
emptyDescription: Create a token to call the public API for this workspace.

scopes.clients:write: Create and update clients, contacts and deals
scopes.files:read: Read file metadata and issue download links

webhooksDescription: Send signed event payloads to an HTTPS endpoint when projects, tasks, CRM records or members change.
createEndpointDescription: Choose the events this endpoint receives. The signing secret is shown once.
editEndpointDescription: Change the URL, events or active state. The signing secret stays the same.
deleteEndpointDescription: Deliveries stop immediately and the endpoint is removed from this workspace.
secretDescription: Use this secret to verify X-Asynchrone-Signature. It is shown only once.
noWebhooksDescription: Add an endpoint to receive signed events.
deliveriesDescription: Every webhook attempt, with its response and retry state.
noDeliveriesDescription: Deliveries appear here once an event is sent to an endpoint.

docs.title: REST API
docs.description: Read and write your workspace data from scripts and integrations with a scoped API token.
docs.metadataDescription: Organization-scoped REST API for Asynchrone Space: projects, tasks, clients, contacts, deals, employees and files.
docs.authDescription: Create a token in Settings → Developers and send it as Authorization: Bearer async_…. The raw value is shown once; revoking it takes effect immediately.
docs.scopesDescription: A token only carries the scopes you select. A write scope never bypasses the member's current role.
docs.endpointsDescription: Every endpoint is scoped to the token's organization.
docs.paginationDescription: Lists accept limit (1–100, default 50) and an opaque cursor. meta.nextCursor is null on the last page and meta.hasMore mirrors it.
docs.errorsDescription: Failures use a stable envelope. error.code is machine-readable and meta.requestId identifies the request in the logs.
docs.rateLimitsDescription: Limits are per token and per plan: 60 requests per minute on Free, 300 on Team and 1,200 on Enterprise. Responses carry X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining and X-RateLimit-Reset; a 429 includes Retry-After.
